title: Redwood PLG quickstart discovery - Oxford Cloud
summary: Intro discovery focused on Redwood quickstart / self-serve API. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for chat/embedding use cases. Discussed free credits, time-to-first-token, SSO/KMS requirements, latency vs cost tradeoffs, pilot benchmarks, and next steps: share pricing, security pack, schedule SE-led perf deep dive, start trial.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
latency vs cost, batching and caching
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kumar (Redwood SE), John Ellis (Oxford CTO), Priya Nair (Head of Infra), Samir Patel (ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] John: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:12] Maya: great, quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the quickstart team, Ravi with me is our systems SE, we'll run through our quickstart flow, free credits, and then talk about hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:25] Priya: hi all, Priya here, run infra at Oxford Cloud, want to understand security and data residency.
[00:33] Samir: Samir, ML eng, mostly interested in latency and embedding costs.
[00:40] Ravi: awesome, quick agenda, 1) show quickstart time-to-first-token 2) discuss capacity options 3) run through security checklist 4) next steps. Sound good?

[02:05] John: yeah, we're evaluating a couple vendors, but biggest things for us are time-to-first-token for devs, predictable cost for inference, and being able to choose private deployment if needed.

[03:10] Maya: totally, that's what we hear a lot. Our PLG quickstart gives free credits — you can get started in minutes with SDK or curl. We also have a hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved pools for throughput SLAs, and Private for VPC/on-prem.

[04:45] Samir: what's the average time to first token for devs? like from signup to a sample chat response.

[05:02] Ravi: typically under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart — sign up, API key in console, run the example request. Demo caveat: depends on model size and whether streaming is used. For a base chat model it's usually < 3s latency for small prompts on hosted, though your network hops matter.

[06:20] Priya: ok but in prod we care about p95 latency under 200ms for short prompts. Is that realistic on hosted?

[06:36] Ravi: p95 under 200ms is tight for hosted for many open models, it's more achievable with Dedicated pinned capacity and smaller quantized variants. We can also do prefix caching and batching tweaks to get closer. There's a tradeoff — cost goes up as you optimize latency.

[07:40] John: Can you quantify cost delta between hosted and dedicated?

[07:55] Maya: ballpark — hosted is pure usage pricing, good for early dev and low volume. Dedicated is monthly reserved capacity which reduces per-token unit cost and gives predictable throughput; typical customers see 30-60% unit cost reduction at scale but commit to baseline. We can share a pricing sheet.

[09:10] Samir: what's involved to try private deployment? we have some regulated workflows where data can't leave our VPC.

[09:25] Ravi: for private we offer a customer-managed control plane and VPC connectors, or on-prem package for air-gapped. It requires coordination for networking, KMS integration for keys, and a short deployment window. We usually do a pilot deployment with a dedicated infra runbook.

[10:40] Priya: KMS — do you support our cloud KMS? we use AWS KMS with external key policies.

[10:50] Ravi: yes, AWS KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated with BYOK flows; also HSM integrations are possible. For hosted we manage keys but we can do customer-managed keys in some enterprise plans.

[12:00] John: security — SOC2 and audit logs, SSO?

[12:10] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II (note: transcription may say SOC-two), and we provide audit logs, RBAC, SAML/SSO integration for workspace access. We'll share our security pack and SOC2 report.

[13:20] Samir: from an ML perspective, can we test throughput and latency with benchmarks on our payload?

[13:34] Ravi: absolutely, we run pilot benchmarks. We can spin up a short Dedicated trial or you can run hosted with a workload generator — we have a benchmark harness and a shared spreadsheet to log results. We'll need your prompt sets and average sequence lengths.

[15:00] John: what about model variants and quantization? we need embeddings for search and chat for assistants.

[15:12] Ravi: Embeddings are lower latency; for search at scale we recommend dedicated pools and 8-bit quantized models often hit sweet spot on cost/quality. For chat, we recommend RLHF-aligned variants or Redwood-curated models. Note: sometimes model names are transcribed oddly in notes — e.g., Redwood Quickstart model lineup.

[16:45] Priya: Do you handle data retention and logs? we need logs for 90 days and deletion controls.

[16:58] Maya: hosted offers configurable retention; enterprise plans include longer retention and deletion controls, plus audit export. Private gives you full control.

[18:30] Samir: latency vs cost — can you explain batching and KV cache? I heard KV cash in a thread and we're not sure what that is.

[18:45] Ravi: KV cache — Key-Value cache holds token context across calls so warm starts are faster. Batching groups small requests to utilize GPU throughput; both reduce cost but can increase single-request latency if you wait to batch. We have auto-batching heuristics to balance SLOs.

[20:05] John: competitors — we've looked at OpenAI, Anthropic, and AWS Bedrock. How do you differentiate?

[20:18] Maya: high-level: we focus on production inference economics — unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, transparent benchmarks, and tooling to tune batching/quantization for cost. We'll share benchmark comparisons, though specific numbers vary by model and workload.

[22:30] Priya: governance — can we restrict models allowed in org? we don't want people hitting large costly models by accident.

[22:42] Ravi: yes, RBAC and per-route model whitelisting, quotas and rate limits per team — console controls this.

[24:00] Samir: for a PLG quickstart, what are the common gotchas?

[24:10] Maya: sign-up friction (SSO vs email), missing prompt templates, and not pinning model versions. Also forgetting to set quotas which leads to surprise costs. We provide quickstart templates and free credits to explore safely.

[25:50] John: how much free credit do you usually give?

[26:00] Maya: default trial credits are $300 for self-serve, can be extended for pilot commits. For dedicated pilots we sometimes offer credit against reserved capacity.

[27:30] Priya: can devs get up and running without SSO? we need an SSO onboarding plan but don't want to block devs.

[27:42] Maya: yes, self-serve uses email sign-up initially, you can later enforce SSO. We'll provide a template for migrating accounts to SSO.

[29:10] Ravi: quick demo — code snippet for calling text generation, note streaming support and function calling. (Ravi pastes a sample request)

[29:40] Ravi: "curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{...}'" — if you run that after signup you should see a response in seconds.

[31:00] Samir: and embeddings endpoints?

[31:10] Ravi: /v1/embeddings with batching support; there are SDK helpers to do efficient batching to reduce latency and cost.

[32:20] John: for the pilot, we want to test 10k embedding calls per day and 200 concurrent chat sessions. Is that feasible on hosted?

[32:35] Ravi: hosted can handle that but your p95 SLA won't be guaranteed; Dedicated reserved pools are better for guaranteed throughput. We can recommend pool sizes once we see your RPS and token distribution.

[34:00] Priya: any restrictions on bringing our own models? we use some custom fine-tuned models internally.

[34:12] Ravi: we can host customer models on Dedicated or Private; hosted allows some customer models via model onboarding but has a review process. On-prem setups are best for fully private models.

[35:40] John: what's the timeline for a Dedicated pilot?

[35:50] Maya: typically 2-4 weeks setup for a small reserved pool including network, KMS, and model variants — 4-6 weeks if private with more networking. We'll scope exact dates after the SE deep dive.

[37:10] Samir: any bench numbers you can share now? e.g., tokens/sec for 8-bit 7B model on a single GPU?

[37:25] Ravi: rough numbers: an optimized 7B quantized model can do ~200-300 tokens/sec on an A10x type instance under our runtime; 13B is slower. These are workload dependent — we'll run your prompts to get exacts.

[39:00] Priya: compliance question — do you support customer-managed audit log exports to our SIEM?

[39:12] Maya: yes, we provide log export to S3 or syslog endpoints in enterprise plans. We'll include examples in the security pack.

[40:30] John: ok let's talk next steps.

[40:35] Maya: proposed next steps: 1) I'll send pricing and security pack 2) Ravi will run a perf checklist and propose pilot sizing 3) schedule a SE-led benchmark session where Oxford provides prompts — sound right?

[41:10] Priya: yes and include the KMS/Network runbook.

[41:30] Samir: also send the quickstart link and the SDK examples.

[41:45] Maya: will do. Anything else?

[42:10] John: can you put estimated costs for the 10k/day embedding and 200 concurrent chat in the pricing sheet?

[42:25] Maya: yes we'll add a sample cost projection.

[43:50] Ravi: tiny note — sometimes transcripts mess up acronyms, so if you see V-P-C or KV cash in the notes, that's me saying VPC and KV cache.

[44:20] Maya: cool, recapping: send pricing, security pack (SOC2, audit log samples, KMS guide), quickstart links, schedule SE benchmark next week, Oxford to share prompt sets.

[45:00] John: great, appreciate it.

[45:15] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with calendar invites.

[46:00] (small chatter as people drop)

[47:30] End of meeting.
